methods.label: Complete an enclosing square
methods.explanation:
The octagon's equal interior angles each measure
\[
\frac{(8-2)180^\circ}{8}=135^\circ,
\]
so its boundary turns by \(45^\circ\) at every vertex. Orient one length-\(1\) side horizontally. Successive length-\(1\) sides are separated by two such turns, so the four length-\(1\) sides alternate between horizontal and vertical.

Extend these four sides until neighboring horizontal and vertical lines meet. They enclose a rectangle, with one triangle outside the octagon at each corner. Each corner triangle has angles \(45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ\), so its legs are equal. Its hypotenuse is a short side of the octagon, of length \(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\). If each leg has length \(x>0\), the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
2x^2=\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)^2=\frac12,
\qquad x=\frac12.
\]
Each side of the enclosing rectangle therefore has length \(\frac12+1+\frac12=2\), making it a square. Subtracting the four corner triangles gives the octagon's area:
\[
2^2-4\left(\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12\right)
=4-\frac12=\boxed{\frac72}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
